name: Territory navigation and evidence disclosure
description: A user can find a state and county, inspect an EMS/fire account, and understand that imported account-level metrics may be modeled.
steps: Open the home page and navigate to National Geographic Explorer or Territory
Choose Florida, then a county, then inspect an available EMS or fire provider account
Read the provider evidence notice and return to the geographic directory
expected: The directory responds to geographic filters; an account opens and displays an unverified-data warning instead of treating a model-generated fleet, buyer, grant, or outcome as confirmed evidence.

name: Federal NPI legal-identity check
description: The check presents a genuine exact-identity match or a clearly unverified result, never a fabricated NPI.
steps: Open a provider profile through the geographic directory
Inspect the validation result and any source warning
expected: A match displays its CMS NPI legal-entity origin; an unmatched entity remains explicitly unverified. No NPI, procurement contact or clinical outcome is invented.

name: Research desk returns open map lookup
description: The research assistant operates on mobile and clearly identifies geographic searches as unverified links.
steps: Open the Research desk on a mobile viewport
Choose Nearby facilities and type 'trauma center'
expected: The assistant shows an OpenStreetMap search link and a warning that the result is not a verified hospital; no Google sign-in or Google Maps window is required.

name: Authenticity and storage health dashboard
description: The data-health panel reports actual backend connection and scoped storage state, not fake cloud snapshots.
steps: Navigate to Data Integrity or Cloud Resilience from the workspace
Refresh live backend health and read the remote records status
Inspect the email sign-in option and absence of Google sign-in
expected: The health panel reflects real service status; without an authenticated account it clearly says remote writes have not been verified; no fabricated restore-point history appears.

name: Authenticated field notes and territory research
covers: notes and bookmarks persist through reload
description: A signed-in user can save a note and stage/bookmark changes, create a custom agency where offered, and use the AppDeploy research assistant.
setup: Use an authenticated AppDeploy email-link test account; complete email-link verification before starting the test
steps: Open an EMS/fire provider, add a unique field visit note and bookmark it
Reload the page, return to the same account, and inspect the note and bookmark
Use the account research desk to request a clinical briefing; if custom-agency creation is available, create one and confirm it appears after reload
expected: Saved notes and bookmarks persist in the signed-in account without Google services; the briefing displays caveats about unverifiable details; a custom account, if created, is restricted to that user and labeled unverified.
